device_status: Read the phone's RAM, storage, thermal state, and inference accelerators.
memory_search: Search Bram's persistent memory across conversations for facts and earlier work.
write_file: Write a file into Bram's private files area at a relative path (overwrites).
list_files: List files in Bram's private files area, newest last.
read_file: Read a file from Bram's private files area, truncated beyond 64 KB.
clipboard_get: Read the current clipboard text. The clipboard may be unreadable while Bram is backgrounded.
clipboard_set: Put text on the system clipboard, replacing what is there.
post_notification: Show a notification from Bram in the status shade.
schedule_notification: Schedule a notification for a future time, e.g. a reminder.
launch_uri: Open a URI (http, tel, mailto, geo) in whatever app handles it.
search_contacts: Search device contacts by name; returns names and phone numbers.
read_calendar_events: Read calendar events between two epoch-millis times.
propose_skill: Draft a skill — a short reusable procedure — for the user to review and activate. Drafts are not active until approved.
write_note: Write a short note to Bram's private storage under a given name.
list_skills: List installed skills (active and drafts) as name, version, and description.
read_skill: Read one active skill's instructions, in chunks; pass nextOffset to continue. Read before following a skill.
termux_exec: Run a command in Termux; returns exit code, stdout, and stderr. Prefer `shell` (a bash line) for anything that chains or pipes — its working directory persists across calls in a conversation; use `command`+`args` for one executable with verbatim arguments. Output is truncated near 50 KB per stream. Requires Termux with external-app access.
tool_search: Find tools by what they do when the one you need is not offered; returns names, descriptions, and schemas.
get_weather: Current weather and daily forecast for any place. Use for every weather question — never web_search or web_fetch.
web_search: Search the public web (DuckDuckGo); returns title, URL, and snippet. Only for current or factual information no purpose-built tool covers.
web_fetch: Download one web page and return its text with HTML stripped. Use after web_search has picked a URL to read.
